blocks.text: Marketing insights are knowledge and understanding about a market, its consumers and companies. They are generated by observing behaviour (data collection and analysis of behaviours, lifestyles, markets and cultures) and are fundamental to understand a marketplace and identify emerging trends.

children: providing a deeper understanding of consumer behaviour and its drivers
tracking changes in consumer needs and desires
understanding how different consumer groups perceive the world and culture around them

blocks.text: Key moments for insights: looking back (historical data), the present (real-time tracking, e.g. Voice of Customer, NPS) and looking forward (trend forecasting, statistical modelling). Marketing research ≠ marketing insights – research is one tool for discovery.

Primary research is collected for a specific purpose (experimental or non-experimental, qualitative or quantitative). Secondary research uses already compiled internal or external data and is usually more time- and cost-effective. The research process: problem → sources & design → method → collection → analysis.
A market analysis is a quantitative and qualitative assessment of a market:
Useful databases: Euromonitor International, LS:N Global, Statista, Xerfi.

A consumer trend is a new manifestation – in behaviour, attitude or expectation – of a fundamental human need, want or desire. Trend forecasting combines intuition, hard data and experience. Macro trends last at least five years across industries; micro trends reach mass adoption within one to two years.

children: Basic needs: fundamental, rarely changing human needs
Drivers of change: there are no trends without change
Innovations: examples of how a trend exists – not trends themselves

blocks.text: To identify trends, forecasters look for weak signals, practise cultural brailling and run horizon scanning (STEEPLE). They review previous trends, research known future events, describe the current situation, analyse unexpected events and identify common threads.
Evaluate trends for opportunity along trend maturity, locality and industry.
The Consumer Trend Canvas turns insights into innovation:
children: ANALYSE: inspirations, basic needs, drivers of change (shifts and triggers), emerging consumer expectations
APPLY: innovation potential (vision, business model, product/service/experience, marketing) and who (customer groups, personas)

blocks.text: The capacity to gain an accurate and deep understanding of someone or something (Oxford).
An anomaly that is overlooked by mainstream organisations because it is vague; it becomes meaningful when organised in clusters across industries.
Faith Popcorn's term for sampling and sensing change in the way consumers live, on a daily basis.
A structured, contextualised approach to detect shifts in the social, technological, economic, environmental, political, legal and ethical landscape.
New, unmet needs, wants and desires created by innovations and change; found in the gap between what consumers want and what they have.
A rich description of one fictional person exemplifying a specific group of people.
